clue.text: Pleasant Democrat potentially a senator?

blocks.note: D is the standard abbreviation for a Democrat
someone who could win a vote and become a senator is fit to be chosen

explanation.surface: A genial American politician who might one day sit in the Senate.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'potentially a senator' is a fanciful description of a word meaning able to win an election.
explanation.definitionFit: Something delectable is delightful or delicious, a close synonym of pleasant.

clue.text: Mug's in arrears, without a penny

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: money that is overdue is due
p is the abbreviation for a penny

explanation.surface: A sucker who is behind on his payments and broke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' reads as lacking, but here it means outside. Mug is British slang for a gullible fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A dupe is someone easily fooled, which is what a mug means in British slang.

clue.text: He works a bit, using metal in job, right?

indicators.note: the metal is placed inside the word for an occupation

blocks.note: one's line is one's trade or occupation
or is gold in heraldry
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A part-time worker asking whether a metalwork job is right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Works a bit' sounds like a part-timer; a bit is a horse's mouthpiece, which this craftsman makes. Or is the heraldic word for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A loriner is a maker of bits, spurs and other metal fittings for horse harness.

clue.text: Affectedly fashionable person disturbed her host in the end

indicators.note: something disturbed is jumbled out of order
the jumbled letters are placed inside the closing word

blocks.note: these seven letters rearranged
the close is the end of something

explanation.surface: A dandy guest who has upset the woman throwing the party.
explanation.definitionFit: A clothes-horse is someone who cares too much about fashionable dress, by extension from the drying frame.

clue.text: Eagerness to construct a real city out east

indicators.note: constructing builds something new from the materials given
out says the compass point is left out of the material

blocks.note: the letters taken as written
E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Keen planners eager to build a genuine city out in the east.
explanation.definitionFit: Alacrity is brisk and cheerful readiness to do something, a close synonym of eagerness.

clue.text: Show promise and seek a reference

blocks.note: first meaning: to improve, as when things start to brighten
second meaning: to search for something in a dictionary or book

explanation.surface: A job applicant who shows potential and asks for a referee.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to start improving and to consult a reference work for information.

clue.text: Eat out in estaminet cheaply

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words that follows, spanning a word break

blocks.note: the last letters of the first word run on into the first letters of the second

explanation.surface: Dining out at a cheap French café.
explanation.walkthrough: An estaminet is a small French bar-café, which makes 'Eat out' look like dining; here it means corrode, as acid does to metal.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to cut a design by letting acid corrode the surface, so it eats away at the metal.

clue.text: Fruit taste the Spanish love

blocks.note: a tang is a sharp taste
el is Spanish for the
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A Spaniard who adores the flavour of a certain fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangelo is a citrus hybrid of tangerine and pomelo or grapefruit.

clue.text: Outstanding features of Oxford Street illuminations

blocks.note: the main street of Oxford is known as the High
illuminations are decorative lights

explanation.surface: The best bits of the Christmas lights display on London's Oxford Street.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford Street is London's shopping street famous for its lights, but here it is the main street in the city of Oxford, called the High.
explanation.definitionFit: Highlights are the most notable or memorable parts of something, its standout moments.

clue.text: Filter from by-pass approaching a hill

indicators.note: approaching means drawing up next to, so the hill piece follows straight on

blocks.note: per means by, as in per post
a col is a mountain pass
taken as written
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A road sign for a by-pass leading up towards a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By-pass' reads as one road but splits into by and pass; 'approaching' just puts the pieces next to each other.
explanation.definitionFit: A percolator is a coffee maker that passes water through grounds, a kind of filter.

clue.text: Comfortable with arms folded back

indicators.note: folding something back turns it round so it runs the other way

blocks.note: arms in the sense of weapons

explanation.surface: Sitting at ease, arms folded behind one's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Snug describes being cosy, warm and at ease, which matches comfortable.

clue.text: He speculatively considers the Creation, I recollected

indicators.note: re-collected means gathered up again in a new arrangement

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A thinker musing on the origins of the universe, as I recall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recollected' reads as remembered, but split as re-collected it means gathered again.
explanation.definitionFit: A theoretician deals in theory and abstract speculation rather than practical work.

clue.text: Island bird's heading off

indicators.note: a word's heading is its first letter, and off says it is removed

blocks.note: a finch is a small songbird; the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A bird on an island taking flight.
explanation.walkthrough: Inch is a Scottish word for a small island, common in place names such as Inchcolm.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland and Ireland an inch is a small island, a crossword-friendly regional sense.

clue.text: Hooligan appears to hand out harsh treatment

blocks.note: a rough is a violent lout
to deal is to hand out, as with cards

explanation.surface: A thug handing out a beating to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough deal is unfair or harsh handling of someone, an everyday idiom.

clue.text: Killjoy finds profit suppressing drink

indicators.note: in a down entry, pressing down on something means sitting above it

blocks.note: spoils are gains or plunder
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: A party pooper who confiscates the booze to make money.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoilsport ruins other people's fun, exactly what a killjoy does.

clue.text: Mistletoe held up by host, for example

definitions.text: Mistletoe held up by host, for example

blocks.note: surface reading: someone at a party holding mistletoe aloft for kisses
setter's reading: mistletoe grows on a host tree, which supports it and feeds it

explanation.surface: A Christmas party host raising a sprig of mistletoe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Host' suggests a party giver, but in biology the host is the tree that mistletoe lives off.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistletoe draws water and nutrients from the tree it grows on, which makes it a textbook plant that lives off another.

clue.text: Farewell excessively drawn out

blocks.note: first meaning: an informal goodbye
second meaning: of such great length

explanation.surface: A goodbye that goes on far too long.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a casual parting word, and read literally it describes something of tiresome length.

clue.text: Partiality is a failing

blocks.note: first meaning: a fondness, as in a soft spot for chocolate
second meaning: a fault or flaw in character

explanation.surface: A judge declaring that bias is a flaw.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a special liking for something and a defect or shortcoming.

clue.text: Wild animal's back at home, first approaching stream

indicators.note: going back means the creature's name is read from its end
says the home piece comes first and the creature follows straight after it

blocks.note: being in means being at home
a wolf is a wild animal

explanation.surface: A wild creature returns to its den, heading for the stream.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflow is a stream of water or other matter flowing into a place, so a stream in noun form.

clue.text: Decline to mock scapegoat

blocks.note: to fall is to drop or decline
to guy someone is to ridicule them

explanation.surface: Refusing to mock someone who is being blamed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline' looks like refuse, but it means a drop.
explanation.definitionFit: A fall guy takes the blame for others' wrongdoing, exactly what a scapegoat is.

clue.text: Having a proper bearing, about to take off

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
to levant is to abscond, especially to skip off without paying debts

explanation.surface: A dignified figure just about to set off on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: Levant as a verb is an old British word for running away from one's debts.
explanation.definitionFit: Something relevant bears on the matter in hand, so it is pertinent or connected to it.

clue.text: Changed over after a mile

indicators.note: after says this word comes behind the opening pieces

blocks.note: taken as written
M is the abbreviation for mile
something over has finished

explanation.surface: A runner switching places after the first mile of a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' looks like a direction or a cricket term but means finished.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend something is to alter or correct it, so amended means altered.

clue.text: Weapon gunners used, covering landing area

indicators.note: in a down entry, covering means sitting on top of the following piece

blocks.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the British army's gunners
a pier is a landing stage for boats

explanation.surface: Artillery troops guarding a beach landing with their guns.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapier is a slender thrusting sword, a classic weapon.

clue.text: Hunt to collect drinks for marketing promotion

indicators.note: collecting things means gathering them inside, so one word goes around the other

blocks.note: to stalk prey is to hunt it
ales are beers, a kind of drink

explanation.surface: A hunting party gathering refreshments for a publicity event.
explanation.definitionFit: Sales talk is the persuasive patter used to push a product, a spoken form of promotion.

clue.text: Chills South with lead of diamonds

indicators.note: says the gem piece leads, placed before the compass point

blocks.note: ice is slang for diamonds
S is the abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: A bridge player in the South seat leads a diamond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South' and 'lead of diamonds' sound like a bridge deal; diamonds are ice in thieves' slang.
explanation.definitionFit: To ice something is to make it cold, so ices works as a verb meaning chills.

clue.text: Little boy in a whirl

blocks.note: first meaning: a pet form of the name Edward
second meaning: a swirling current of water or air

explanation.surface: A small child spinning round in a dizzy state.
explanation.definitionFit: Eddy is a diminutive of Edward, and an eddy is a circular swirl in water or air.

clue.text: Gory mayhem in wild party

indicators.note: mayhem is chaos, so the preceding word's letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Bloody chaos breaking out at a riotous party.
explanation.definitionFit: An orgy is an unrestrained bout of revelry and indulgence, a wild party.

clue.text: Liberal president objected, holding similar views

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for Liberal
Ike was the nickname of US President Eisenhower
if you minded something, you objected to it

explanation.surface: A progressive president raising objections in a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: People who are like-minded share the same opinions and tastes.

clue.text: Trifles enjoyed in the nursery

blocks.note: first meaning: as a verb, plays idly with
second meaning: playthings small children have fun with

explanation.surface: Puddings served up as a treat in a children's nursery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trifles' looks like the dessert or small things; it is the verb, toying with something.
explanation.definitionFit: To toy with something is to trifle with it, and toys are the playthings children use.

clue.text: Time for our revolution to succeed here and now

indicators.note: succeeding means coming after, so the time piece follows the other

blocks.note: someone here is present
the Earth turns once in a day

explanation.surface: A rebel declaring the moment has come for the uprising to win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolution' suggests an uprising, but it is the Earth spinning round once.
explanation.definitionFit: Present-day describes the current era, things of this moment, so it stands for now used as a modifier.
